references.text: Joseph's advice to Pharaoh on finding a discerning and wise man to rule over Egypt – the immediate context for the proposal to appoint overseers.
The continuation of Joseph's plan: to gather all food during the good years and store grain in the cities, so that the land would not perish during the famine.
The result of Joseph's plan during the famine – how he managed Egypt's grain reserves and bought land and people for Pharaoh.
The ant that gathers food in summer and stores provisions in autumn – a wisdom parallel to Joseph's principle of gathering in times of abundance to prepare for times of scarcity.
'Precious treasure and oil are in the house of the wise' – wisdom in storing and preparing for the future.
The parable of the faithful and wise steward who gives the household food at the proper time – a New Testament parallel to Joseph's role as a wise steward over Egypt's food supply.
This reference shows the implementation of the one-fifth system that was proposed in the source verse.
Confirmation of the seven years of abundance as the basis for the one-fifth system.
Shows how the proposed system was made into a permanent law for Egypt.
